requirements.title: Say whether a file was parsed, and why not
requirements.rationale: Four different causes of an empty outline look the same today, and a caller that accepts or refuses an edit has to know which one it has.

criteria.condition: Outline or OutlineMany is given a file whose bytes a backend parses, with or without syntax errors
criteria.action: report the file as parsed by that backend, with no reason, and with an empty, non-nil list of syntax errors when the parse found none
criteria.contract: `File.Parsed == true`, `File.NotParsed == ""`, `File.Backend` is `BackendGoAST` or `BackendTreeSitter`; for a file without syntax errors `len(File.SyntaxErrors) == 0`, `File.SyntaxErrors != nil` and `File.SyntaxErrorsTruncated == false`

check.pseudocode: in outline/goast_test.go, TestOutlineOfAGoFile (testdata/go_sample.go) also asserts f.Parsed, f.NotParsed == "", f.SyntaxErrors non-nil and empty, not truncated; in outline/treesitter_test.go, every case of the table of TestTreeSitterDeclarations (one clean file for each of the fourteen tree-sitter languages, .tsx and a C++ .h) asserts the same with Backend tree-sitter. A helper in outline/helpers_test.go states the assertion once.

criteria.condition: the file's extension is not in the extension table, or the build has no backend for its language (any language but Go in a build without cgo)
criteria.action: report the file as not parsed with the reason `unsupported`, without reading a file whose extension is unknown
criteria.contract: the exported constant for `unsupported` in `File.NotParsed`; `Backend == BackendNone`, `Parsed == false`, `len(Decls) == 0`, `len(SyntaxErrors) == 0` with both slices non-nil, `SyntaxErrorsTruncated == false`; a nil error

check.pseudocode: one table test in outline/outline_test.go over the files that are not parsed, replacing the isNone assertions of TestOutlineOfAnUnknownExtensionReadsNothing, TestOutlineOfAFileOverTheSizeLimitIsNone, TestOutlineOfABinaryFileIsNone and TestOutlineOfAGoFileWithNoSyntaxTreeIsNone with the reason each has: /nonexistent/foo.xyz with nil src -> unsupported and no error (it is not read); a .go file of 501 bytes with MaxFileBytes 500, given and on disk, and a directory named big.py with MaxFileBytes 1 -> too_large; a .go file of exactly 500 bytes with MaxFileBytes 500 -> parsed; a file over 1 MiB with MaxFileBytes 0 -> too_large; a file over the limit that also holds a NUL -> too_large; a NUL in the first 8 KiB -> binary; a NUL after them -> parsed; parseGo replaced to return a nil tree -> failed. isNone in outline/helpers_test.go takes the wanted reason and asserts the whole contract. In outline/treesitter_nocgo_test.go, TestWithoutCgoOnlyGoIsOutlined asserts a.py is Python, unsupported. In outline/treesitter_test.go, a grammar whose query does not compile, put into the grammars table for one language for the length of the test, gives failed.

criteria.condition: the file is larger than Options.MaxFileBytes, or than 1 MiB when that option is zero, whatever its content, given as bytes or on disk
criteria.action: report the file as not parsed with the reason `too_large`, without reading a file on disk that is over the limit
criteria.contract: the exported constant for `too_large` in `File.NotParsed`; `Backend == BackendNone`, `Parsed == false`, `len(Decls) == 0`, `len(SyntaxErrors) == 0` with both slices non-nil, `SyntaxErrorsTruncated == false`; a file of exactly the limit is parsed

criteria.condition: a file within the size limit has a NUL byte in its first 8 KiB
criteria.action: report the file as not parsed with the reason `binary`
criteria.contract: the exported constant for `binary` in `File.NotParsed`; `Backend == BackendNone`, `Parsed == false`, `len(Decls) == 0`, `len(SyntaxErrors) == 0` with both slices non-nil, `SyntaxErrorsTruncated == false`; a NUL byte after the first 8 KiB does not make the file binary

criteria.condition: the backend for the file's language returns no syntax tree while the context is live: the Go parser gives no AST, or a tree-sitter grammar or its query cannot be loaded
criteria.action: report the file as not parsed with the reason `failed`
criteria.contract: the exported constant for `failed` in `File.NotParsed`; `Backend == BackendNone`, `Parsed == false`, `len(Decls) == 0`, `len(SyntaxErrors) == 0` with both slices non-nil, `SyntaxErrorsTruncated == false`; a nil error

criteria.condition: a file given without bytes cannot be read from disk
criteria.action: return an error from Outline, and from OutlineMany return for that input a file that is not parsed with the reason `failed`, the other inputs unaffected
criteria.contract: Outline: the zero `File` and a non-nil error. OutlineMany: a nil error and, at the input's index, a `File` with its `Path` and `Lang`, `NotParsed` the constant for `failed`, `Backend == BackendNone`, `Parsed == false`, `len(Decls) == 0`, `len(SyntaxErrors) == 0` with both slices non-nil, `SyntaxErrorsTruncated == false`

check.pseudocode: in outline/outline_test.go: TestOutlineOfAnUnreadableFileIsAnError stays as it is; TestOutlineManyKeepsTheInputOrder also asserts, per file, Parsed and NotParsed: a.go, d.go and given.go parsed with no reason, missing.py failed, c.unknown unsupported

requirements.title: Report the syntax errors of a Go file
requirements.rationale: go/parser already finds every error and outline throws them away; a caller that refuses an unparseable edit needs them without a parser of its own.

criteria.condition: go/parser, asked for all errors, reports errors for a Go file
criteria.action: report one syntax error for each distinct position the parser reports an error at, however many messages the parser has for that position and however many errors are on one line
criteria.contract: `File.Parsed == true`, `File.Backend == BackendGoAST`; each `SyntaxError` has `Line` (1-based) and `Column` (1-based, in bytes) equal to the line and column of the parser's position; no two entries share a line and column

check.pseudocode: one table test in outline/goast_test.go over Go sources and the exact []SyntaxError each gives, with Options.MaxSyntaxErrors 50: (a) `package a`, a blank line, `func F() {`, a tab and `x := 1`, with no closing brace -> exactly [{4, 9, missing}] (the parser has two messages there), a line at or after the function's last; (b) a zero-length non-nil src -> exactly [{1, 1, missing}], with Parsed true and Backend go/ast; (c) `package a`, `func A() {}`, a function F whose body is fourteen lines `f(1 2)` on lines 6 to 19, `func Z() {}` -> fourteen errors, one on each of the lines 6 to 19, all unexpected; (d) a file with two faults on one line -> an entry for each column

criteria.action: for any position go/parser reports an error at, give the error the kind `missing` when a message at that position starts with `expected '`, naming one token in quotes, and the kind `unexpected` otherwise
criteria.contract: `SyntaxError.Kind` is one of the two exported constants, `missing` and `unexpected`

check.pseudocode: rows of the table of REQ-2.1's test in outline/goast_test.go that assert kinds: `package a`, `var s = "abc` with the string not closed -> {2, 9, unexpected} (`string literal not terminated`); `package a`, a blank line, `var x = `, a blank line, `func G() { y := }` -> the errors include {5, 6, missing} (`expected '('`) and {5, 8, unexpected} (`expected type`, which names no token)

criteria.condition: the Go file is empty: zero bytes given, or a zero-length file on disk
criteria.action: report it as parsed by go/ast with exactly one syntax error, at line 1 column 1
criteria.contract: `Parsed == true`, `Backend == BackendGoAST`, `SyntaxErrors` is exactly one entry with `Line == 1` and `Column == 1`

criteria.condition: a Go file has errors on more than ten lines
criteria.action: return the declarations go/parser recovers when asked for all errors, where the outline of such a file was empty before
criteria.contract: `File.Decls` holds the recovered declarations, sorted as for any file

check.pseudocode: in outline/goast_test.go beside TestABrokenGoFileStillYieldsWhatParses: source (c) of REQ-2.1's table -> shows(f.Decls) == [func A L3-3, func F L5-20, func Z L22-22]

requirements.title: Report the syntax errors of a file parsed by tree-sitter
requirements.rationale: The tree marks what it could not place and what it had to assume, and the outline never looked.

criteria.condition: the syntax tree of a file has an error node with no error node among its ancestors
criteria.action: report one `unexpected` syntax error at the start of that node, and none for an error node inside another error node
criteria.contract: a `SyntaxError` with `Kind` unexpected, `Line` the node's start row plus one and `Column` its start column in bytes plus one

check.pseudocode: one table test in outline/treesitter_test.go over broken sources and the exact []SyntaxError each gives: a.py holding `def f():`, then `    x = ((( ]]] }}} $$ ??`, then `    y = [1, (2, {3: ]` (its tree has four error nodes inside one outer error node) -> exactly [{2, 5, unexpected}]

criteria.condition: the syntax tree of a file has a missing node
criteria.action: report one `missing` syntax error at the position of that node, which is where the token was expected
criteria.contract: a `SyntaxError` with `Kind` missing, `Line` the node's start row plus one and `Column` its start column in bytes plus one

check.pseudocode: rows of the table of REQ-3.1's test in outline/treesitter_test.go: A.java holding `class A {`, `  int x = 1`, `  void m() {}`, `}` -> exactly [{2, 12, missing}]; a.js holding `const x = (1 + 2;`, `let y = 3;` -> exactly [{1, 17, missing}]; a.py holding `def f(:`, `    pass` -> exactly [{1, 7, missing}]

criteria.action: for a file with a syntax error in any of the fourteen tree-sitter languages, in a .tsx file and in a C++ .h header, report the file as parsed by tree-sitter with at least one syntax error whose line is the line of the fault or the line of the first token after it
criteria.contract: `Parsed == true`, `Backend == BackendTreeSitter`, `NotParsed == ""`, `len(SyntaxErrors) >= 1`

check.pseudocode: a table test in outline/treesitter_test.go with one broken file for each file name of TestTreeSitterDeclarations's table (a.py, a.js, a.ts, a.tsx, A.java, a.cs, a.kt, a.scala, a.rs, a.c, a.cpp, a.h, a.php, a.rb, a.lua, a.sh): the clean source of that table with one local fault put on a known line (a parenthesis or bracket left open before the end of a statement, or a stray closing bracket), and the fault's line beside it; assert Parsed, Backend tree-sitter, and that some error has Line == fault line or fault line + 1 when the next token is on the next line

criteria.condition: a tree-sitter parse finds error nodes and missing nodes, more of them together than Options.MaxSyntaxErrors allows
criteria.action: order the two kinds together by position and keep the first ones up to the limit
criteria.contract: `SyntaxErrors` ascending by `Line`, then `Column`; `len(SyntaxErrors)` equal to the limit and `SyntaxErrorsTruncated == true`

check.pseudocode: in outline/treesitter_test.go: a.py holding `def f(:`, `    pass`, a blank line, `def g():`, `    return (1 + ` -> with the default options exactly [{1, 7, missing}, {5, 5, unexpected}], not truncated; with MaxSyntaxErrors 1 exactly [{1, 7, missing}], truncated

requirements.title: Order the syntax errors and stop at a limit
requirements.rationale: A badly broken file can have thousands of errors, and a caller wants the first few.

criteria.action: for any parsed file, return its syntax errors in ascending order of line, then of column
criteria.contract: for every i, `SyntaxErrors[i]` is at a position before `SyntaxErrors[i+1]`

check.pseudocode: in outline/goast_test.go, in the table of REQ-2.1's test: every row asserts the list is strictly ascending by (Line, Column); source (c) gives the lines 6, 7, ... 19 in that order

criteria.condition: a parse finds more syntax errors than Options.MaxSyntaxErrors, or than 20 when that option is zero
criteria.action: keep the first errors in position order up to the limit and say that the list was cut
criteria.contract: `len(SyntaxErrors)` equals the limit and `SyntaxErrorsTruncated == true`; with as many errors as the limit or fewer, all are returned and `SyntaxErrorsTruncated == false`

check.pseudocode: a table test in outline/goast_test.go over (number n of `f(1 2)` lines in the body of F, starting at line 6; MaxSyntaxErrors; wanted length; wanted truncated; wanted last Line): (20, 0, 20, false, 25); (21, 0, 20, true, 25); (21, 50, 21, false, 26); (21, 3, 3, true, 8); (3, 3, 3, false, 8); (21, -1, 20, true, 25); (21, -100, 20, true, 25)

criteria.condition: Options.MaxSyntaxErrors is negative
criteria.action: apply the limit of a zero option, 20
criteria.contract: the same `SyntaxErrors` and `SyntaxErrorsTruncated` as with `MaxSyntaxErrors == 0`

requirements.title: Leave the outline and the tools that show it as they are
requirements.rationale: Stored outlines, tool answers and every program built against outline depend on the declarations and on the two error returns.

criteria.action: for any Go file that does not have errors on more than ten lines, clean or damaged, return the same Path, Lang, Backend and declarations (entries, order, kinds, containers, signatures and line ranges) as before this change

setup: the declarations of broken.go as the unchanged code returns them, recorded before any production edit
check.pseudocode: in outline/goast_test.go: TestOutlineOfAGoFile, TestGoDeclarationsHaveTheirKindContainerAndRange and TestGoSignaturesAreOneLineWithoutTheBody pass with their wanted declarations unedited; TestABrokenGoFileStillYieldsWhatParses asserts the whole shows(f.Decls) of its broken.go, the list recorded from the code before the parser mode changes

criteria.action: for any file parsed by tree-sitter, clean or damaged, return the same Path, Lang, Backend and declarations as before this change, with the `.h` rule for C++ and the `.tsx` rule unchanged

setup: the declarations of the three broken files as the unchanged code returns them, recorded before any production edit
check.pseudocode: in outline/treesitter_test.go: TestTreeSitterDeclarations and TestACppHeaderIsOutlinedAsCpp pass with their wanted declarations unedited; the broken a.py, A.java and a.js of REQ-3.2's rows also assert shows(f.Decls), the lists recorded from the code before the backend reads the tree's errors

criteria.condition: the context has ended before the call, or ends while a file is being parsed
criteria.action: return the context's error and no outline
criteria.contract: Outline returns the zero `File` and `ctx.Err()`; OutlineMany returns a nil slice and `ctx.Err()`

check.pseudocode: TestOutlineOfACancelledContextIsItsError in outline/outline_test.go and the Outline and OutlineMany assertions of TestAParseStopsWhenTheContextEnds in outline/treesitter_test.go pass unedited

criteria.condition: the file they outline has syntax errors or was not parsed
criteria.action: answer with the same text and data as before this change, showing no syntax error and no new reason
criteria.contract: the result text and the result data of both tools are those the code returned before this change, byte for byte

setup: the file_outline text of the broken Go file as the unchanged code renders it
check.pseudocode: in tools/outline_tool_test.go: the existing tests and golden files pass without being regenerated, and a case calls file_outline on a Go file whose function lacks its closing brace and asserts the whole result text, recorded from the code before this change; in tools/symbol_tool_test.go and tools/symbols_test.go the existing tests pass unedited

requirements.title: Answer comment and string spans for Go, and label Go reference hits by them
requirements.rationale: Reference search treats every hit in a Go file as text because Go has no entry in the grammar table, and a consumer without cgo has no spans at all.

criteria.condition: CommentAndStringSpans is given a path with the Go extension, in a build with or without cgo
criteria.action: return the byte range `[start, end)` in src of every line comment, block comment, interpreted string, raw string and rune literal, in source order and not overlapping, taken from Go's tokens
criteria.contract: `ok == true`; for each span `src[start:end]` is the whole token as it stands in src, carriage returns included

check.pseudocode: a table test in outline/gospans_test.go, a file with no build constraint so it runs with and without cgo: /x/a.go holding `package a`, `// c`, then a line with "x", a raw string `r<newline>q`, string('c') and /* b */ -> exactly [[10,14], [23,26], [29,34], [44,47], [49,56]] for the source written out in the test, and for every span src[start:end] starts and ends with the token's delimiters; the same source with CRLF line endings -> the raw string's span runs from its opening backtick to its closing one inclusive, and the line comment's span is `// c`; offsets inside code (the identifier s, the call string) are in no span

criteria.condition: the Go file has syntax errors, among them a literal or a comment that is not terminated, or the context has ended
criteria.action: still answer, with an unterminated raw string or block comment reaching the end of src and an unterminated interpreted string or rune literal ending where its token ends, at the end of its line
criteria.contract: `ok == true`; the last span of a file ending in an unterminated block comment or raw string has `end == len(src)`

check.pseudocode: rows of the table of REQ-6.1's test in outline/gospans_test.go: `package a`, `var u = "open`, `/* never` (32 bytes, no final newline) -> exactly [[18,23], [24,32]]; `package a`, then a raw string opened and never closed over two lines -> one span ending at len(src); `package a`, `func broken( {` -> ok and no spans; any row with a cancelled context -> the same answer

criteria.condition: CommentAndStringSpans is given a Go path and an empty or nil src
criteria.action: answer that the file has no spans
criteria.contract: `len(spans) == 0` and `ok == true`

criteria.action: for any path that is not a Go file, answer CommentAndStringSpans as before this change: from the language's tree-sitter grammar with cgo, and with `ok == false` without cgo, without a grammar for the language, or when the context ended

check.pseudocode: in outline/treesitter_test.go, TestCommentAndStringSpans passes with its six language cases unedited and loses its last assertion, that Go has no spans; TestAParseStopsWhenTheContextEnds passes unedited; in outline/treesitter_nocgo_test.go, TestWithoutCgoOnlyGoIsOutlined keeps asserting ok == false for /x/a.py

criteria.condition: a lexical reference search scans a Go file, in a build with or without cgo
criteria.system: reference scanner in the tools package
criteria.action: label a whole-identifier hit outside every comment and string `lexical`, and keep a hit inside a comment or a string in the result, labelled `text`
criteria.contract: `ReferenceSite.Confidence` is `lexical` or `text`; the sites' paths, lines, columns and sources are as before

check.pseudocode: in tools/ref_scanner_test.go, TestACodeHitIsLexicalAndACommentOrStringHitIsText gains a Go file that needs no cgo: scanContentForMatches(`t.go`, src, Decl{Name: `Marshal`}) for `package t`, `// Marshal is deprecated`, `var s = "Marshal"`, `func f() { yaml.Marshal(nil) }` -> confidences [text, text, lexical] at lines 2, 3 and 4, in every build

criteria.system: reference search in the tools package
criteria.action: for any target a Go package of the workspace declares, return the sites go/types resolves, and for any search with the `text` backend label every site `text`, both as before this change

check.pseudocode: in tools/find_references_test.go and tools/references_test.go: TestFindReferencesResolvesAGoMethodsCallers, TestReferencesFindsTheResolvedCallers and TestReferencesChoosesItsBackendFromTheTarget pass with their wanted sites and result text unedited; TestFindReferencesOfANameNothingDeclaresIsText gains a Go file with the name in code and asserts that site is `text` too

execution_paths.title: A program outlines a clean file, then one it has just broken

steps.action: calls outline.Outline with the bytes of a Python file that has no syntax error
parses the bytes with the tree-sitter Python grammar and returns the declarations with Parsed true and no syntax errors
removes the closing brace of a function in a Go file and calls outline.Outline with the new bytes
parses them once with go/parser, all errors requested, and returns the declarations the parser recovered with Parsed true and a syntax error at or after the function's last line
refuses the edit because the list of syntax errors is not empty

real_components: the tree-sitter Python grammar, in a cgo build
setup: a cgo build; outline/testdata/go_sample.go as the Go file
end_state: the Python file: Backend tree-sitter, Parsed, its declarations, zero syntax errors
the Go file after the edit: Backend go/ast, Parsed, a non-empty Decls, and at least one syntax error with Line at or after the last line of the function that lost its brace
smoke.pseudocode: in outline/treesitter_test.go (cgo): f = Outline(ctx, /x/a.py, clean); assert f.Parsed && f.Backend == BackendTreeSitter && len(f.Decls) > 0 && len(f.SyntaxErrors) == 0; src = bytes of testdata/go_sample.go with the closing brace of Greet (line 6) removed; g = Outline(ctx, go_sample.go, src); assert g.Parsed && g.Backend == BackendGoAST && len(g.Decls) > 0 && len(g.SyntaxErrors) > 0 && every error's Line >= 6

execution_paths.title: A program is told why a file was not parsed

steps.action: calls outline.Outline with the path of a 2 MiB JavaScript file on disk and the default options
finds the size over the limit on the stat, does not read the file, and returns Parsed false with the reason too_large, no declarations and no syntax errors
tells the reason apart from a clean file and from an unsupported one

setup: a 2 MiB file named big.js in a temporary directory
end_state: Parsed false, NotParsed too_large, Backend none, no declarations, no syntax errors, a nil error
smoke.pseudocode: in outline/outline_test.go: write 2<<20 bytes of `//x` lines to dir/big.js; f = Outline(ctx, dir/big.js, nil, Options{}); assert err == nil && !f.Parsed && f.NotParsed == the too_large constant && f.Lang == LangJavaScript && len(f.Decls) == 0 && len(f.SyntaxErrors) == 0; and the same call for a clean dir/a.go gives Parsed with NotParsed empty

execution_paths.title: The same program built without cgo

steps.action: is built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and calls outline.Outline for a Python file and for a Go file with a syntax error
returns the Python file as not parsed with the reason unsupported
returns the Go file as parsed by go/ast with its declarations and its syntax errors, and answers CommentAndStringSpans for it

real_components: the outline package built with CGO_ENABLED=0
setup: CGO_ENABLED=0 in the environment of the test run
end_state: `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -short -count=1 ./outline/...` passes, and in that run: a.py is Python, not parsed, unsupported; a Go file without its closing brace is parsed with a syntax error; CommentAndStringSpans answers ok for the Go file and not ok for a.py
smoke.pseudocode: run `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -short -count=1 ./outline/...`; it compiles outline/treesitter_nocgo_test.go, whose TestWithoutCgoOnlyGoIsOutlined asserts the three end states through Outline and CommentAndStringSpans, and the Go tests of goast_test.go and gospans_test.go, which have no build constraint

execution_paths.title: A reference search tells a Go call from a Go comment

steps.action: calls tools.References for the name Marshal, which no Go package of the workspace declares
finds no Go declaration of the name, chooses the lexical backend and scans the files that mention it, a Go file among them
answers CommentAndStringSpans for the Go file from its tokens
returns the call `yaml.Marshal` as lexical and the line `// Marshal is deprecated` as text, the lexical site first

setup: a workspace with go.mod and one Go file that imports an external yaml package, calls yaml.Marshal and has the comment line `// Marshal is deprecated`
end_state: Backend lexical; two sites in the Go file: the call with Confidence lexical, then the comment line with Confidence text; the same in a build without cgo
smoke.pseudocode: in tools/references_test.go: ws = newWS(t, {go.mod, enc/enc.go}); res = References(ctx, ws, outline.Decl{Kind: KindFunc, Name: `Marshal`}, ReferenceOptions{}); assert res.Backend == `lexical` && siteList(res) == [enc/enc.go:<call line>:<col> lexical, enc/enc.go:<comment line>:4 text]
